clue.text: Crossbar broken by headers from Erling Haaland is put up again

indicators.note: something broken by another thing is split open with that thing lodged in the gap

parts.note: a rung is a crossbar on a ladder or chair

indicators.note: headers are the tops of things, so only the opening letters of the two names are wanted

parts.note: first letters of the footballer's two names

explanation.surface: A football crossbar, smashed by Erling Haaland's headers, gets put back up.
explanation.walkthrough: Haaland is a Norwegian striker famous for scoring, so 'headers' reads as football, but it means the first letters of his names.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rehung, like a door or a picture, has been hung up again after being taken down.

clue.text: Revolutionary Chinese New Year for each part of Russian Federation

parts.note: Che Guevara, the archetypal revolutionary
a standard abbreviation for Chinese
N for new and Y for year
as in 'ten pounds a head', a means for each

explanation.surface: A revolutionary Chinese New Year celebration held in each region of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Chechnya is a republic in the North Caucasus that forms one of the constituent subjects of the Russian Federation.

clue.text: Stallion stripped off for girl of 19

indicators.note: stripped means peeled of its outer layer, so the word loses its first and last letters
off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: A stallion has its saddle stripped off for a young rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 refers to 19 down, the author NABOKOV, so the girl of 19 is the title character of his novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is the title girl of Vladimir Nabokov's 1955 novel, so she is the girl belonging to that author.

clue.text: Green is one with secure seat

parts.note: greens are green vegetables, and a bean is one of them
to bag something is to secure or capture it

explanation.surface: A Green Party politician, one of them, secures a safe parliamentary seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green is one' reads as a politician of the Green Party; really it defines by example, a bean being one of the greens on your plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanbag is a large soft bag filled with beads or beans, used as a floor seat.

clue.text: Grace Kelly ultimately supporting lover with tango

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or admirer
tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the name is kept

parts.note: last letter of the name

explanation.surface: Grace Kelly, the film star, backing her lover in a tango.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Kelly the actress is one surface name; the clue splits her, so Grace is the definition and Kelly supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace and beauty are near synonyms for elegant loveliness of form or movement.

clue.text: Worried voices about the heart of Manchester United

indicators.note: worried means agitated and disturbed, so the letters are shaken into a new order
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the middle piece

parts.note: rearranged

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letters are taken

parts.note: the two central letters of the ten-letter city name

explanation.surface: Anxious voices among supporters about the state of Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester United reads as the football club; the two words have separate jobs, with United the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohesive group sticks together as one, which is to say it is united.

clue.text: Topples in shortened pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or badly done, so the word is mangled into new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone falls over while wearing trousers cut too short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortened pants' looks like cut-down trousers; in British slang pants is also an adjective meaning rubbish, which makes it the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dethrone a ruler is to remove them from power, as to topple them is.

clue.text: Criminal following X-Man?

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
Elon Musk, owner of the social network X

explanation.surface: A criminal who follows one of the Marvel X-Men superheroes.
explanation.walkthrough: X-Man suggests the Marvel mutants; the question mark flags the twist that it means the man who owns X, formerly Twitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone convicted of a serious crime, so a criminal.

clue.text: Works in ointment to stop case of fleas

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: outer letters of the word
an unction is an ointment used for anointing

explanation.surface: Rubbing ointment into a pet's coat works to stop an outbreak of fleas.
explanation.walkthrough: Works reads as a verb in the surface, but here it is a plural noun or verb matching the answer: something that works, functions.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that works is one that functions; the two verbs mean operate properly.

clue.text: Radio Four's back on air

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

parts.note: last letter of the number word

explanation.surface: BBC Radio Four is back on the air after an outage.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio Four is a BBC station, but the clue splits the name: Radio is the definition and Four supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuner is a radio receiver, especially one forming a unit in a hi-fi system.

clue.text: Nick Drake essentially in love

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, as nil is in football

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so the middle letter of the name is taken

parts.note: the central letter of the name

explanation.surface: Nick Drake, the folk singer, was at his core a man in love.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Drake was an English singer-songwriter; the clue splits his name, with Nick as the definition in its slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to nick a suspect is to arrest them, and to nail someone means to catch them too.

clue.text: Witch doctor in Guinea exhausted after migraine oddly

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first in the answer
oddly picks out the letters in odd-numbered positions

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied, so the word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the word with its insides emptied out

explanation.surface: A witch doctor in Guinea is worn out after a strange migraine.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinea reads as the West African country in the surface, which fits the witch doctor, but it is just a word to be emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Mganga is the Swahili word for a traditional healer or medicine man in East Africa.

clue.text: Obsessive sibling welcoming year in therapy

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: anal in the Freudian sense means obsessively fussy
sis is short for sister
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: An obsessive brother or sister who has spent a year in therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Analysis is short for psychoanalysis, the talking therapy, as in being in analysis.

clue.text: Isaac Hayes initially confused about piano mute?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go around the musical abbreviation
confused means muddled, so the letters are mixed up into new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the surname is taken

parts.note: first letter of the surname
p is the musical notation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: Soul singer Isaac Hayes, bewildered at first, standing silent by the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: an aphasic person has lost language, which can leave them unable to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphasia is loss of the ability to produce or understand speech after brain damage, so a sufferer may be effectively without words.

clue.text: Writer covering match in the shade

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around, so the outer piece encloses the other

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
two accounts that match agree

explanation.surface: A writer covering a cricket match while sitting in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Match suggests a sporting fixture to report on; it is the verb, meaning correspond.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea-green is a shade of bright yellowish green, the colour of fresh peas.

clue.text: Tax-free vehicles concealed by Lisa Stansfield

indicators.note: concealed by means tucked away inside the following words, so the letters run across them

parts.note: found running across the singer's two names

explanation.surface: Pop singer Lisa Stansfield hiding her tax-free cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Lisa Stansfield is an English soul singer. An ISA, Individual Savings Account, is a UK tax-free savings scheme; 'vehicles' is used in its investment sense.
explanation.definitionFit: ISAs are British savings accounts whose interest is exempt from tax, so they are tax-free investment vehicles.

clue.text: King touring desert in chopper

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the outer piece goes round the other

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
to desert someone is to leave them

explanation.surface: A king flying around the desert in a helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopper suggests a helicopter to fit the desert tour; it is the butcher's knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is a heavy broad-bladed knife used for chopping meat, so a chopper.

clue.text: Barney Rubble's opening a Nutmeg cryptic

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and obscure, so the letters are scrambled
opening means the start, so only the first letter of the name is taken

parts.note: first letter of the name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Barney Rubble from The Flintstones opens a Guardian crossword by the setter Nutmeg.
explanation.walkthrough: Barney Rubble is one cartoon name; split, Barney is the definition, British slang for a noisy quarrel. Nutmeg is a fellow Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A barney is an informal British word for a heated row, which is an argument.

clue.text: Author served up very fine port

indicators.note: in a down answer, served up means sent upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: v is the abbreviation for very
OK means fine or all right
Oban is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A writer is served a glass of very fine port.
explanation.walkthrough: Port reads as the fortified wine being served; it is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was the Russian-American writer of Lolita and Pale Fire, an author.

clue.text: Relish chicken pad thai regularly

parts.note: a capon is a castrated cockerel raised for eating

indicators.note: regularly picks letters at even intervals, here every second one

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone savours a dish of chicken pad thai on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: Relish looks like a verb meaning enjoy; it is the noun, a savoury accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: Caponata is a Sicilian sweet-and-sour aubergine dish often served as a relish or side.

clue.text: 24 across getting awards

indicators.note: the number stands for the answer at that light, crack, which means break up and so signals rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another clue that somehow wins awards.
explanation.walkthrough: '24 across' looks like an ordinary cross-reference; read 24 as its answer, CRACK, and the clue says crack the word across.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscars are the Academy Awards given annually for achievement in film.

clue.text: Bouncer in row about horse?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer in a row about a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouncer suggests a nightclub doorman; the question mark points to the bouncy tiger in Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigger, the tiger in A. A. Milne's Pooh stories, is forever bouncing, so he is a famous bouncer.

clue.text: Ordered secure document for auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the words are to be judged by sound

parts.note: tied means secured, and an ID is an identity document

explanation.surface: Instructions to lock up a document before the accountant's audit.
explanation.walkthrough: Auditor suggests an accountant checking the books; literally it means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidied room has been put in order, so tidied and ordered both mean arranged neatly.

clue.text: Heart of Mexico's team

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its two middle letters are taken

parts.note: the two central letters of the country's name

explanation.surface: The core of the Mexican national football side.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters read as a Roman numeral, which is then written out as the number word.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket team has eleven players, so a team is called an eleven.

clue.text: Try first-rate drug

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an attempt, as in have a go
second meaning: expert or elite, as in troops
third meaning: a crystalline form of cocaine

explanation.surface: Someone urges another to sample some top-quality narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings rather than two: have a crack at it, a crack shot, and the street drug.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a noun for an attempt, an adjective for excellent, and a noun for smokable cocaine.

clue.text: Tory ended up admitting motorway declared dangerous

indicators.note: up here means in disarray, as in things being all up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the mixed letters take in another piece

parts.note: rearranged
M as in M1, a British motorway

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician ended up approving a motorway that was ruled unsafe.
explanation.definitionFit: A building condemned by inspectors has been officially pronounced unfit or unsafe to use.

clue.text: Bryan Singer's boat

definitions.note: a name: the surname of the singer Bryan
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Bryan, the Roxy Music frontman, is a singer with this surname
second meaning: a vessel carrying passengers across water

explanation.walkthrough: Bryan Singer is a film director, which is the misdirection; read it as 'Bryan the singer', the Roxy Music vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferry is a boat that carries passengers and vehicles across a stretch of water on a regular route.

clue.text: Be subjected to terrible Mud encore

indicators.note: terrible means awful or wrecked, so the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An audience forced to sit through a dreadful encore by the band Mud.
explanation.walkthrough: Mud were a 1970s British glam-rock band, best known for Tiger Feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To come under criticism or attack is to be subjected to it, a fixed idiom.
